Grafana's IRSA service account uses a namespace string without waiting for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. When namespace creation is enabled, the service account can be created before its namespace exists.

fix.expression: { name = var.kubernetes_service_account, namespace = var.create_kubernetes_namespace && var.kubernetes_namespace != "kube-system" ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa[0].metadata[0].name : var.kubernetes_namespace, annotations = var.irsa_iam_policies != null ? { "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.irsa[0].arn } : null }

diagnostics.message: Spark History Server's service account does not wait for the namespace created alongside it, allowing a namespace-not-found creation race.

fix.expression: { name = var.kubernetes_service_account, namespace = var.create_kubernetes_namespace && var.kubernetes_namespace != "kube-system" ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa[0].metadata[0].name : var.kubernetes_namespace, annotations = var.irsa_iam_policies != null ? { "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.irsa[0].arn } : null }

diagnostics.message: Prometheus Helm installation uses local.namespace_name rather than the created namespace and has no dependency on kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus. With create_namespace absent from helm_config, Helm does not create the namespace itself and can race its creation.

fix.expression: merge({ name = local.name, chart = local.name, version = "15.10.1", repository = "https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts", description = "Prometheus helm Chart deployment configuration", values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { operating_system = try(var.helm_config.operating_system, "linux") })] }, var.helm_config, { namespace = local.create_namespace ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus[0].metadata[0].name : local.namespace_name })

The ADOT add-on waits for RBAC roles but not kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot. The binding must exist before the EKS add-on manager can exercise the namespaced permissions required for installation.
The ADOT add-on waits for the cluster role but not its binding. Installation can begin before the EKS add-on manager receives its required cluster-wide permissions.
